dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:5401.text: The hand-length of an average woman, eight cun, is called 咫: the Zhou chi. Formed from 尺, with 只 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5402.text: Small or fine. Formed from inverted 毛 behind 尸. Some ancient people tied on tails as ornaments; the southwestern Yi do likewise. All characters in this group follow 尾. The present clerical transformation is 尾.

shuowen:5403.text: To connect. Formed from 尾, with 蜀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5404.text: Without a tail. Formed from 尾, with 出 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5405.text: Human urine. Formed from 尾 and 水.

shuowen:5406.text: What the feet rest upon. Formed from 尸, 彳 and 夊; 舟 depicts the shoe’s shape. Another explanation: 尸 indicates the sound. All characters in this group follow 履.

shuowen:5407.text: Footwear. Formed from abbreviated 履, with 婁 indicating the sound. Another explanation: leather shoes.

shuowen:5408.text: The underside of footwear. Formed from abbreviated 履, with 歴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5409.text: A kind of footwear. Formed from abbreviated 履, with 予 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5410.text: Clogs, 屐. Formed from abbreviated 履, with 喬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5411.text: Footwear, 屩. Formed from abbreviated 履, with 支 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5412.text: A boat. In antiquity Gonggu and Huodi hollowed wood into boats and sharpened wood into oars to cross otherwise impassable places. Pictographic. All characters in this group follow 舟.

shuowen:5413.text: Hollowing the middle of wood to make a boat. Formed from 亼, 舟 and 巜; 巜 means water.

shuowen:5414.text: A boat. Formed from 舟, with abbreviated 鉛 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5415.text: A boat moving. Formed from 舟, with 彡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5416.text: The stern or length of a boat, 艫. Formed from 舟, with 由 indicating the sound. Han law calls a boat’s breadth and length 舳艫. Another explanation: the stern.

shuowen:5417.text: Part of 舳艫. Another explanation: the bow of a boat. Formed from 舟, with 盧 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5418.text: A boat moving unsteadily. Formed from 舟 and abbreviated 刖. Read like 兀.

shuowen:5419.text: A boat grounded and unable to move. Formed from 舟, with 㚇 indicating the sound. Read like 䔂.

shuowen:5420.text: I or me. Further explanation is missing.

shuowen:5421.text: A boatmaster. The Bright Hall Monthly Ordinances mentions “舫 men,” those skilled in water. Formed from 舟, with 方 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5422.text: To turn aside. Depicts a boat turning, hence 舟, together with 殳, the means of turning it.

shuowen:5423.text: To use. Another explanation: the right-hand outrunner horse of a carriage, enabling it to turn. Formed from 舟, with 𠬝 indicating the sound. The wording 所以舟旋 is uncertain.

shuowen:5424.text: A boat. Formed from 舟, with 可 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5425.text: A small boat. Formed from 舟, with 廷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5426.text: 艅艎, a boat name. Formed from 舟, with 余 indicating the sound. The classics also use 餘皇.

shuowen:5427.text: The boat 艅艎. Formed from 舟, with 皇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5428.text: Boats joined side by side. Depicts two abbreviated 舟 with their bows joined. All characters in this group follow 方.

shuowen:5429.text: Boats joined side by side. Formed from 方, with 亢 indicating the sound. The Rites prescribes: the Son of Heaven uses a bridge of boats; feudal lords, linked boats; grand officers, paired boats; officers, a single boat.

shuowen:5430.text: A benevolent person; an unusual ancient-script form of 人. Pictographic. Confucius says: “Being below others, therefore bent.” All characters in this group follow 儿.

shuowen:5431.text: High and flat on top. Formed from 一 above 人. Read like 敻. Maoling has Wusang Neighborhood, 兀桑.

shuowen:5432.text: A young child. Formed from 儿, depicting the still-open fontanel of a small child’s head.

shuowen:5433.text: Trustworthy. Formed from 儿, with 㠯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5434.text: Pleased. Formed from 儿, with 㕣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5435.text: To grow; tall. Formed from 儿, with abbreviated 育 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5436.text: Elder. Formed from 儿 and 口. All characters in this group follow 兄.

shuowen:5437.text: To compete. Formed from two 兄, conveying competition, with 丯 indicating the sound. Read like 矜. Another explanation: 兢 means reverent.

shuowen:5438.text: A hairpin for the head. Formed from 人, with 匕 depicting a hairpin. All characters in this group follow 兂.

shuowen:5439.text: 朁朁, intent and eager in purpose. Formed from two 兂.

shuowen:5440.text: Facial appearance and bearing. Formed from 人, with 白 depicting a person’s face. All characters in this group follow 皃.

shuowen:5441.text: A ceremonial crown: Zhou calls it 覍, Yin 吁, Xia 收. Formed from 皃; pictographic.

shuowen:5442.text: To obstruct and cover. Formed from 人, depicting both sides covered. All characters in this group follow 𠑹. Read like 瞽.

shuowen:5443.text: 兜鍪, armor for the head. Formed from 𠑹 and abbreviated 皃; 皃 depicts a person’s head.

shuowen:5444.text: To advance ahead. Formed from 儿 and 之. All characters in this group follow 先.

shuowen:5445.text: To advance. Formed from two 先. 贊 follows this element. Further explanation is missing.

shuowen:5446.text: Without hair. Formed from 人, with the upper part depicting grain and taking its sound. All characters in this group follow 禿. Wang Yu says Cangjie went out and saw a bald man crouching in grain, and made the graph from this. Its accuracy is unknown.

shuowen:5447.text: A bald appearance. Formed from 禿, with 貴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5448.text: To see. Formed from 儿 and 目. All characters in this group follow 見.

shuowen:5449.text: To look at. Formed from 見 and 示.

shuowen:5450.text: To seek. Formed from 見, with 麗 indicating the sound. Read like 池.

shuowen:5451.text: To look favorably or beautifully. Formed from 見, with 委 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5452.text: To look sideways. Formed from 見, with 兒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5453.text: To look favorably or carefully. Formed from 見, with 𤔔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5454.text: To look with a smile. Formed from 見, with 录 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5455.text: To look broadly or intently. Formed from 見, with 爰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5456.text: To inspect closely. Formed from 見, with 㶣 indicating the sound. Read like 鎌.

shuowen:5457.text: To look broadly outward over many things. Formed from 見, with 員 indicating the sound. Read like 運.

shuowen:5458.text: To look attentively. Formed from 見, with 雚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5459.text: To take. Formed from 見 and 寸; 寸 means measuring and also represents a hand.

shuowen:5460.text: To view. Formed from 見 and 監; 監 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5461.text: To look inward. Formed from 見, with 來 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5462.text: Manifest. Formed from 見, with 是 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5463.text: The eyes examining and perceiving. Formed from 見, with 票 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5464.text: 𧠥覰, to peep and watch. Formed from 見, with 𠂔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5465.text: 拘覰, not yet close or thorough. Formed from 見, with 虘 indicating the sound. The precise descriptive phrase is uncertain.

shuowen:5466.text: To see only a little. Formed from 見, with 冥 indicating the sound. The Erya says: “覭髳, not separated”; the quoted expression is uncertain.

shuowen:5467.text: To look inward. Formed from 見, with 甚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5468.text: To encounter and see. Formed from 見, with 冓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5469.text: To fix one’s eyes on something. Formed from 見, with 歸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5470.text: To spy. Formed from 見, with 占 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “The duke sent someone to spy on it; it was true.”

shuowen:5471.text: To watch over. Formed from 見, with 微 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5472.text: To appear briefly. Formed from 見, with 炎 indicating the sound. The Gongyang Commentary on the Spring and Autumn says: “Suddenly there was Prince Yangsheng.”

shuowen:5473.text: To appear briefly. Formed from 見, with 賓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5474.text: Briefly appearing, 䚔𧢜. Formed from 見, with 樊 indicating the sound. Read like 幡.

shuowen:5475.text: An ill person’s manner of looking. Formed from 見, with 氐 indicating the sound. Read like 迷.

shuowen:5476.text: To look down into depth. Formed from 見, with 𠧴 indicating the sound. Read like 攸.

shuowen:5477.text: To put one’s head out secretly and look. Formed from 見, with 䑣 indicating the sound. Read like 郴.

shuowen:5478.text: To jut forward. Formed from 見 and 𠔼.

shuowen:5479.text: To hope for a fortunate chance. Formed from 見, with 豈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5480.text: To desire. Formed from 見, with 俞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5481.text: To see unclearly. Another explanation: to stare straight ahead. Formed from 見, with 舂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5482.text: To see mistakenly. Formed from 見, with 龠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5483.text: To awaken. Formed from 見, with abbreviated 學 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to reveal.

shuowen:5484.text: Red eyes. Formed from 見, with abbreviated 𥏼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5485.text: To summon. Formed from 見, with 青 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5486.text: To arrive or be close. Formed from 見, with 亲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5487.text: The feudal lords’ autumn court audience is 覲, acknowledging their royal service. Formed from 見, with 堇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5488.text: The feudal lords’ great exchange of visits every three years is 頫; 頫 means to see. Formed from 見, with 兆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5489.text: To choose. Formed from 見, with 毛 indicating the sound. Read like 苗.

shuowen:5490.text: Concealed so as not to see one another. Formed from 見, with 必 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5491.text: To watch a person. Formed from 見, with 它 indicating the sound. Read like 馳.

shuowen:5492.text: Dirt obscuring the eyes. Formed from 見, with 𠁁 indicating the sound. Read like 钙.

shuowen:5493.text: To see. Formed from 見, with 𧸇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5494.text: To look side by side. Formed from two 見. All characters in this group follow 覞.

shuowen:5495.text: To stare fiercely. Formed from 覞, with 肩 indicating the sound. Duke Jing of Qi had a brave minister named Cheng 𧢞.

shuowen:5496.text: Seeing rain and together coming to rest; the phrase 比息 is uncertain. Formed from 覞 and 雨. Read like 欷.

shuowen:5497.text: Opening the mouth and releasing breath; the wording 气悟 is uncertain. Depicts breath rising out of a person. All characters in this group follow 欠.

shuowen:5498.text: The appearance of yawning. Formed from 欠, with 金 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5499.text: The appearance of yawning. Formed from 欠, with 䜌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5500.text: Joyful. Formed from 欠, with 吉 indicating the sound.
